dimensions.a: $299 — four printers for the price of one Prusa.
dimensions.b: $949+ — you're buying longevity, not specs.
dimensions.why: Nothing in 2026 beats the Centauri on value. Nothing.

comparisons.verdict: The honest answer: the Centauri Carbon gives you 80% of the printing for 25% of the money. The CORE One+ earns its premium in year three, when it's still printing perfectly and every part is still available. Buy the Prusa if you can afford to think in decades.

comparisons.title: Elegoo Centauri Carbon vs Snapmaker U1

Elegoo Centauri Carbon.name: Elegoo Centauri Carbon
Elegoo Centauri Carbon.best_for: Budget engineering prints — carbon fiber on a budget
Elegoo Centauri Carbon.summary: The 2026 budget disruptor: enclosed CoreXY, 500mm/s, 320°C nozzle that handles carbon-fiber filaments — at one-third the price of a P2S. No multicolor on v1, smaller community, unbeatable value for functional prints.

Snapmaker U1.name: Snapmaker U1
Snapmaker U1.best_for: Multi-color printing without the purge waste
Snapmaker U1.summary: The consumer toolchanger: 4 independent direct-drive toolheads swap in ~5 seconds with near-zero purge waste. Brilliant for multi-color work; open frame needs the $149 Top Cover for ABS/ASA/PA.

dimensions.b: Open frame: PLA/PETG/TPU until the Top Cover.
dimensions.why: Today, the $299 printer handles tougher filaments than the $899 one.

dimensions.name: 🔧 Simplicity
dimensions.a: One nozzle, one filament path, fewer things to break.
dimensions.b: Four toolheads, four filament paths, beta slicer.
dimensions.why: The Centauri is the simpler, more reliable machine right now.

comparisons.verdict: Different tools: the Centauri is the unbeatable budget workhorse for functional single-color prints; the U1 is the multi-color specialist. If you don't need multi-color, save $600 and buy the Centauri.

Prusa CORE One+.best_for: Reliability-first buyers, open-source, repairable for a decade
Prusa CORE One+.summary: Prusa's CoreXY flagship: 55°C active chamber, 300°C nozzle (400°C with HT upgrade), fully open-source and user-repairable, no cloud account required. The buy-it-for-a-decade printer.

Snapmaker U1.best_for: Multi-color printing without the purge waste
Snapmaker U1.summary: The consumer toolchanger: 4 independent direct-drive toolheads swap in ~5 seconds with near-zero purge waste. Brilliant for multi-color work; open frame needs the $149 Top Cover for ABS/ASA/PA.

dimensions.b: Open frame until Top Cover; 300°C max.

dimensions.a: Prusa's legendary consistency, parts for years.
dimensions.b: First-gen toolchanger; long-term durability unproven.
dimensions.why: The CORE One+ is the safe pair of hands.

dimensions.a: Printables, decades of trust.
dimensions.b: Post-Kickstarter energy, growing fast.

comparisons.verdict: The reliability-first buyer takes the CORE One+ without hesitation. The multi-color-obsessed buyer takes the U1 and accepts first-gen quirks. There's no wrong answer — only different priorities.
